strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: The Rust runtime can recover eligible replace_file items from latest recorded partial multi-file transaction evidence through proposal.apply.
Recovery is admitted only after source transaction fingerprint revalidation, applied-item revalidation, approval freshness, target hash, path, file kind, symlink, content, and diff gates.
Recovery apply results record bounded source transaction and item evidence without raw replacement content, raw diffs, or paths outside workspace-relative summaries.
Headless callers can move from partial transaction failure evidence to an explicit recovery apply result without owning recovery policy outside the runtime.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: proposal.apply can execute a bounded recovery mutation for failed or not-applied replace_file items from a latest recorded partial transaction.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M14.1 records transaction failures but has no runtime-owned recovery admission or source fingerprint revalidation.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Autonomous callers can still stall after partial multi-file mutation or implement unsafe caller-side recovery policy.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M14.1 added multi-file transaction apply; M14.2 adds recovery from its partial-failure evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing side-effecting proposal.apply authority is extended with transaction_recovery_source.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result extends bounded apply result evidence tied to actual mutation rather than adding an inspection/report surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime revalidates partial transaction evidence, verifies already-applied items, admits recovery targets, and writes recovered files.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Controllers can recover from a partial transaction by passing bounded source evidence and receive deterministic denial or applied outcomes.
answers.milestone_progress: Pairs M14's first multi-file transaction execution with a recovery path for its primary failure mode.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M14.2 updates the deterministic current phase manifest. Review must confirm real transaction recovery mutation behavior, not a recovery report or guard-only phase.

exit_criteria: A latest recorded partial multi-file replace transaction can admit an explicit recovery request
Successful recovery mutates only eligible failed or not-applied replace_file items
Bad, stale, missing, non-partial, or already-recovered source evidence rejects before writing
Already-applied source items are revalidated and are not silently rewritten

Recovery result and ledger payloads contain bounded source transaction metadata but no raw content, diffs, patches, raw request bodies, absolute paths, canonical paths, stdout, stderr, commands, environment values, API keys, or secrets
Existing M14.1 transaction apply and M6 single-file apply behavior remains compatible
No new RPC, diagnostics wrapper, readiness report, digest, history, preview, automatic recovery, shell, git, network, or service execution is added
next_phase_candidate_notes: After M14.2 merge, assess M14 closeout before adding create/delete/mixed transaction support; do not add a transaction recovery report wrapper.
